entries.definition: able to continue without exhausting the resources it depends on
entries.example: A sustainable plan considers maintenance as well as the first purchase.

entries.definition: the variety of living things in an area or on Earth
entries.example: The survey examines biodiversity rather than counting only the largest animals.

entries.definition: living things and their physical surroundings interacting as a system
entries.example: A change in water quality can affect the whole ecosystem.

entries.definition: the protection and careful management of natural resources or living things
entries.example: The conservation project combines habitat protection with community discussion.

entries.definition: keeping something valuable from damage or loss
entries.example: The plan prioritizes preservation of the remaining old woodland.

entries.definition: work intended to return a damaged environment toward a healthier state
entries.example: The wetland restoration began with a study of water flow.

entries.definition: a decline in the condition or quality of an environment
entries.example: The team investigated soil degradation around the unused road.

entries.definition: the wearing away and movement of soil or rock
entries.example: Plant cover can help reduce erosion on a slope.

entries.definition: the removal of forest so land has another use
entries.example: The map compares areas affected by deforestation over time.

entries.definition: establishing trees again where forest has been removed
entries.example: The reforestation plan includes long-term care for the planted trees.

entries.definition: a substance or energy released into the environment
entries.example: The report identifies the source of each major emission.

entries.definition: an atmospheric gas that absorbs and releases heat radiation
entries.example: The diagram explains why methane is a greenhouse gas.

entries.definition: fuel formed from ancient organic material underground
entries.example: Coal is a fossil fuel used in some energy systems.

entries.definition: an estimate of greenhouse-gas emissions associated with an activity or product
entries.example: The carbon footprint estimate depends on which stages are included.

entries.definition: a gas composed of carbon and oxygen
entries.example: The lesson follows carbon dioxide through several natural and human processes.

entries.definition: a gas made of carbon and hydrogen found in natural and human systems
entries.example: The inspection checked the pipe for a possible methane leak.

entries.definition: action intended to reduce the severity of a problem
entries.example: Flood mitigation can involve planning as well as physical barriers.

entries.definition: to change in response to different conditions
entries.example: Farmers may adapt planting choices when local conditions change.

entries.definition: to fill a supply again after it has been reduced
entries.example: Rain can help replenish water stored in the ground.

entries.definition: a situation in which there is not enough of a needed resource
entries.example: Water scarcity affects how the community plans its gardens.

entries.definition: a reduction in a resource through continued use or loss
entries.example: The report examines groundwater depletion over several seasons.

entries.definition: liquid waste discharged from a process or facility
entries.example: The facility tests its effluent before it is released.

entries.definition: a substance that makes something impure or unsafe
entries.example: The laboratory looked for a specific contaminant in the water.

entries.definition: capable of causing harm through poisonous effects
entries.example: The label warns that the substance can be toxic to aquatic life.

entries.definition: involving a risk of harm or danger
entries.example: Hazardous waste needs handling appropriate to its risks.

entries.definition: able to be broken down by living processes under suitable conditions
entries.example: A biodegradable label does not explain how quickly an item breaks down everywhere.

entries.definition: decomposed organic material used to improve soil
entries.translation: کود حاصل از تجزیهٔ مواد آلی
entries.example: The gardener mixed mature compost into the planting area.

entries.definition: a place where waste is deposited for long-term disposal
entries.example: The local plan aims to send less material to landfill.

entries.definition: the controlled burning of waste
entries.example: The report compares incineration with other waste-management options.

entries.definition: an economic approach aimed at keeping materials and products in use
entries.example: Repair and reuse are important ideas in a circular economy.

entries.definition: the use of resources, goods, or energy
entries.example: The meter helps the household track electricity consumption.

entries.definition: the act or process of getting rid of unwanted material
entries.example: The notice explains safe disposal of damaged batteries.

entries.definition: removing a useful substance from its source
entries.example: Water extraction must be considered alongside local supply and demand.

entries.definition: removing minerals or other geological materials from the ground
entries.example: The discussion examined both the benefits and environmental costs of mining.

entries.definition: supplying water to land to help crops grow
entries.example: The farm tested a more carefully controlled irrigation system.

entries.definition: the growing of crops and raising of animals for human use
entries.example: The exhibition explores how agriculture depends on soil and water.

entries.definition: preparing land and growing plants on it
entries.example: The field’s history of cultivation helped explain its soil condition.

entries.definition: a substance added to supply nutrients for plants
entries.example: The gardener checked the soil before choosing a fertilizer.

entries.definition: a substance used to control organisms considered pests
entries.example: The label explains how the pesticide must be handled.

entries.definition: an animal that carries pollen between flowers
entries.example: The students observed a pollinator visiting several flowers.

entries.definition: land where water strongly influences the soil and living community
entries.example: The wetland holds different plants from the dry field beside it.

entries.definition: an area of land draining water toward a shared outlet
entries.example: A problem upstream can affect communities across the watershed.

entries.definition: water stored below the ground in spaces in soil and rock
entries.example: The village monitors groundwater as well as the nearby stream.

entries.definition: water that flows over land instead of soaking into it
entries.example: Heavy rain carried runoff from the paved area toward the drain.

entries.definition: particles carried by water or wind and later deposited
entries.example: The jar contained a layer of sediment after the muddy water settled.

entries.definition: relating to land beside the sea
entries.example: The coastal community plans for changing weather and tides.

entries.definition: relating to the sea and its living systems
entries.example: The museum explains how pollution can affect marine habitats.

entries.definition: relating to land rather than water
entries.example: The study compares terrestrial and aquatic environments.

entries.definition: naturally originating in a particular place
entries.example: The garden favors plants indigenous to the region.

entries.definition: spreading in a new environment and causing ecological harm
entries.example: The volunteers learned to identify the invasive plant before removing it.
